signals.notes: Explicit gap row so the coverage failure is machine-visible. The required series copper.supply-restrictions-routing (owner: this orb) is UNUSABLE: no accepted connector vintage exists in this run and no primary government/customs tonnage series was retrievable (USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026 copper chapter returned HTTP 403). The pre-policy base the MODULE_RULES section 9 bridge must start from (copper.mine-prepolicy-supply, owner commodity-supply) was also not produced this run, so no percentage share of world supply is derivable and none is claimed. Bridge totals for restricted, stranded, rerouted and globally accessible supply are all not_assessable. Zero strength, neutral, non-voting.

THE POLICY KILLER RISK, and it is deliberately emitted as direction=neutral because it is a two-sided binary, not a one-way threat. Proclamation 10962 (signed 2025-07-30, Federal Register doc 2025-14893 published 2025-08-05) required Commerce to update the President on domestic copper markets BY 2026-06-30 so he could decide whether to impose the recommended phased universal duty on REFINED copper of 15% from 2027-01-01 and 30% from 2028-01-01. As of 2026-08-28 the deadline has passed with no proclamation and no new ruling date: 59 days late (2026-06-30 to 2026-08-28, my arithmetic). Expiry is null because the event is genuinely undated and cannot be calendared. Bull flip (section 17, capable of failing): a Federal Register proclamation imposing a refined duty of at least 15% effective on or before 2027-01-01, measured against the 0% refined-cathode duty status quo in force since 2025-08-01 - nothing has been published, so the trigger is not already satisfied. Bear flip: a published determination not to impose, or 2027-01-01 arriving with no duty in force. Sizing context, NOT re-voted here (the COMEX-LME premium is causally owned by commodity-price-curve under regional-premiums and is referenced, not re-emitted): premium 19.2 US cents/lb mid-Aug-2026 = US$423/t at 2204.62 lb/t (my arithmetic), reported at ~8.4x its 2005-2025 average, which implies an average of ~US$50/t; the sibling orb separately measured +US$547/t on 2026-08-26; peak ~US$2,937/t late-Jul-2025; ~US$400/t early Jun-2026. This is NOT a proven critical risk under MODULE_RULES section 11 and must not be used to force Avoid.

The opposing fact, emitted separately rather than netted against the killer-risk row. A market-implied read puts only a 14.6% chance that the recommended 15% refined-copper tariff takes effect on 2027-01-01, rising to 37% for a 30% duty by 2028-01-01, with a long-run COMEX-over-LME bias of only ~US$33/t and a spread mean-reversion half-life of ~3.5 days. Broker research, verdict-stripped per MODULE_RULES section 2, read via a secondary summary (FXStreet) rather than the note itself. Direction is bearish because if the market is right, the current premium is transient and the ex-US price does not permanently lose the metal now sitting in the US.

50% Section 232 duty on semi-finished copper products and copper-intensive derivatives, effective 2025-08-01. Refined cathode, ore, concentrate, matte, anode and copper scrap are EXEMPT from this measure, so it removes ZERO refined tonnes from world supply - hence direction neutral for the metal. Modified by a proclamation signed 2026-06-01, effective 2026-06-08 through 2027-12-31: assessment moves to full customs value and products containing 15% or less steel/aluminium/copper fall out of scope; the 2027-12-31 date is why expiry is set. DATE CONFLICT NOT RESOLVED: a separate secondary summary instead dates a full-value 50%-on-semis / 25%-on-derivatives regime to 2026-04-06 (10% where at least 95% of the metal is US-sourced). I did not reconcile the two against the Federal Register; under CLAUDE.md section 4 the conservative common ground is that the 50% semis tariff is in force on either reading.

Scheduled, not yet implemented. Proclamation 10962 authorised Commerce to require 25% of high-quality US copper scrap to be sold domestically plus an export-licensing requirement, and a domestic-sales requirement for copper input materials (ore, concentrate, matte, cathode, anode) of 25% in 2027, 30% in 2028 and 40% in 2029. Direction bullish for ex-US refined copper because it would remove US scrap feed from the seaborne market (largely China), and bearish for the US domestic scrap discount - two different price legs, stated separately rather than blended. Expiry set to the 2027-01-01 scheduled start, which is the point at which the entry either becomes a live restriction or lapses. No implementing Commerce rule was sourced this run, so the tonnage effect is not measurable.

The only countable restricted tonnage in this register, and it is SMALL - the strength is deliberately low to stop a loud headline voting like a large one. DRC joint ministerial order signed 2026-06-29 with immediate effect prohibits export of copper AND cobalt concentrates; one-year waivers permitted in strategic circumstances; three-month transition to a new by-product tax regime. Size: Q1-2026 DRC exports were 696,725 t of cathode versus 53,926 t of concentrate containing 18,863 t of copper metal, i.e. concentrate was 2.6% of copper in reported export streams; annualised upper bound ~75 kt/yr contained Cu (my arithmetic). Share inference, printed so it can be checked: 0.026 x 0.14 (DRC share of world mined copper, 2025) = ~0.36% of world mined copper, NOT the 14% a headline implies. Concentrate blocked at the border can be smelted domestically (Kamoa-Kakula 500 kt/yr, ~60% utilised in Q1-2026) and exported as unrestricted cathode - that is a change of product FORM inside one country, not a rerouted cargo, so no rerouting is credited. Bull trigger: extension to cathode, or waivers refused to the large operators. Bear trigger: broad waivers or suspension - this is the fourth iteration of the same policy (2013, 2019, 2023, 2026) and the earlier ones did not hold. Expiry null because the order is open-ended.

Registered for completeness and scored NEUTRAL for copper on purpose: this is a COBALT measure and must not be counted as a copper restriction. DRC cobalt export quota regime running since October 2025; 2026 ceiling 96,600 t contained cobalt, of which 9,600 t is a strategic quota controlled by the regulator ARECOMS; DRC was 73% of global cobalt mine output in 2025. The only copper transmission channel is indirect - if a cobalt quota forces a copper-cobalt mine to throttle mill throughput, the lost copper is a PRODUCTION fact owned by commodity-supply, not a restriction owned here. No copper tonnage is deducted. Expiry set to the annual ceiling year-end.

Open-ended downstreaming policy: PT Freeport Indonesia has exported no copper concentrate since its last permit expired at end-2024. Scored neutral because the rule changes the FORM in which Indonesian copper leaves (concentrate to domestic-smelted cathode), not the quantity mined. The tonnes actually missing from the 2026 market are missing because of the Grasberg incident (force majeure Sept-2025, phased restart from Q2-2026, pre-incident rates not before 2027) - a production fact owned by commodity-supply - and are deliberately NOT deducted here, to avoid double-counting under MODULE_RULES section 9. The ban is discretionary: in 2025 Indonesia granted a ~1.27 Mt concentrate export quota while charging a higher export duty as a penalty for the smelter delay. Bull trigger: Indonesia holds the line while its smelters are impaired. Bear trigger: a new 1.27 Mt-scale permit, which would relieve seaborne concentrate tightness.

Emitted as NEUTRAL with an explicit zero deduction, because exchange delivery ineligibility is NOT automatically lost production (MODULE_RULES section 9). OFAC determinations of 2024-04-12, effective 2024-04-13: LME and CME may not accept Russian-origin copper produced on or after that date, and US import of Russian-origin copper is prohibited except for metal produced before it. The LME states no Russian-origin copper has been warranted at an LME-listed EU warehouse for over a year, and from 2026-02-25 requires origin attestations (that requirement is written for Russian aluminium in EU warehouses). The metal is still produced and sold; what changed is where it can become a Western warrant. Rerouting to non-sanctioning buyers is the reported mechanism but I obtained NO tonnage, destination, discount, transport-delay or settlement/insurance evidence, so no verified rerouting is credited and no accessibility claim is made either way. Bull trigger: a full EU/UK import ban on Russian refined copper or secondary sanctions on current buyers. Bear trigger: sanctions relief allowing re-warranting.

Resource-nationalism entry with a DATED flip. Cobre Panama has been idle since November 2023, when Panama's Supreme Court ruled the concession law unconstitutional. In 2026 the government is weighing a state mining company taking a 35-40% stake, or a lease model, with a decision expected before end-2026; President Mulino said it would be communicated publicly this year - hence expiry 2026-12-31. Direction bullish because the mine being out is price-supportive. IMPORTANT non-double-counting note: the lost output itself is a PRODUCTION fact owned by commodity-supply and is deducted nowhere in this orb's bridge; what is registered here is the legal/political cause and its dated decision window. The mine's annual capacity was not sourced this run, so its share of world supply is not measurable and none is asserted.

The opposing fact, emitted separately rather than averaged against the suspension row. First Quantum is accelerating restart preparations: by end-June 2026 it had processed 2.1 million tonnes of stockpiled ore for about 3,200 tonnes of contained copper, with a first shipment expected, and expanded the workforce by roughly 1,000. Direction bearish because metal actually moving out of Panama is the de-escalation. Note the asymmetry the numbers show: 3,200 t of contained copper from stockpile processing is a token volume against any plausible full-rate figure, so this row evidences INTENT and momentum, not restored supply.

Strategic-reserve family, and UNQUANTIFIABLE BY CONSTRUCTION - strength is held low for that reason, not because the buyer is small. China's National Food and Strategic Reserves Administration (formerly the State Reserve Bureau) plans to add copper, cobalt, nickel and lithium to state reserves and has made price inquiries and bids; in Feb-2026 the state-backed metals industry body publicly called for more copper in the strategic stockpile. Timing and quantity are officially confidential and are not published, so no tonnage enters the bridge. Bull trigger: a confirmed purchase tender - a buyer that is price-insensitive by mandate. Bear trigger: the same agency SELLING reserves into a price spike, which is its historical playbook and is why this row is not scored higher.

Two Chinese measures pointing the same way and emitted as one row so they cannot vote twice. (1) Import duties cut effective 2025-01-01: refined copper 2% to 0%, copper scrap 1.5% to 0%, with high-purity scrap reclassified out of solid waste under GB/T 38471-2019. (2) The 13% export tax rebate on copper products was cancelled from December 2024, keeping units inside China. Observed effect: China copper scrap imports were 1.24 Mt in H1-2026, up 8.3% year on year. Direction bearish because a widening feed channel eases the concentrate/scrap tightness that supports price; the offsetting factor is stricter reverse-invoicing enforcement, which has tightened compliant DOMESTIC scrap supply, so the net is not one-directional and strength is held low. China activity is a demand input owned by commodity-macro-drivers and is not re-voted here.

Copper was added to the final US Critical Minerals List published 2025-11-07 (60 minerals, 10 new). Read as an ENABLER rather than a measure: it is the statutory hook that makes further permitting support, stockpiling and trade action on copper easier, and it sits underneath the pending Section 232 refined decision. It restricts no tonnes itself, so it contributes nothing to the bridge. Bear trigger: removal at the next list review.

STALE BY 13 MONTHS and marked expired on purpose: this is a recurrence risk, not a live disruption. In late June / early July 2025, blockades in Chumbivilcas by informal miners (CONFEMIN) interrupted concentrate trucking from MMG's Las Bambas (over 320,000 t copper in 2024), Glencore's Antapaccay and Hudbay's Constancia (99,000 t); on-site operations continued. The blockades were lifted and the government subsequently removed 50,565 miners from the REINFO temporary register, leaving 31,560. I could NOT source the current REINFO deadline or any live 2026 blockade, so the expiry date of the underlying regime is not established and no live tonnage is at risk in this run's bridge. Registered rather than dropped because the trigger is a recurring, date-driven inland chokepoint on Peruvian concentrate, and the next deadline is the flip.

Explicit clean-family row, emitted so the absence is machine-visible and is not mistaken for a checked zero. No live maritime chokepoint entry (Hormuz, Suez / Red Sea, Panama Canal, Black Sea) was found for copper in this sweep, and NO free-source flow share (IMF PortWatch or equivalent) for copper through any named chokepoint was retrieved this run. The correct label is 'none found', NOT 'proved zero'. Copper's main seaborne routes run Chile/Peru to Asia across the open Pacific, and DRC metal moves overland to Durban, Dar es Salaam or the Lobito corridor. The two live INLAND logistics constraints (the Peru mining corridor and the DRC border/rail routes) are emitted as their own rows rather than hidden inside this one. Zero strength, neutral, non-voting.
